Hi Sophie / Tom —

Great to be working with you on RapidRetail's self-checkout rollout. As discussed in the demo, the first 72 hours after public launch look like the main risk window for token-level throughput. To keep the site responsive we want to coordinate a short-term rate uplift during the launch spike.

Can you confirm the following by EOD tomorrow?
- Expected peak QPS and tokens/sec per user session (attached is a simple matrix you can fill)
- Peak window start/end (timezone)
- Any traffic shaping (e.g., phased rollout by region) or hard cutover dates

Internal asks:
- Product: confirm whether a temporary soft-limit increase is feasible for this account and any constraints (david_kim@redwood.com)
- Solutions: propose a warm-up/warm-cache plan and fallback model profile to reduce token cost (priyom_das@redwood.com)
- CS/Onboarding: own the user communications and warm-up runbooks (monica_patel@redwood.com)

I've attached a quick traffic matrix you can edit. Ideally we get numbers today so we can lock a temporary uplift and a rollback policy.

Thanks —
Ben

Thanks, attached is the matrix with expected hour-by-hour load for the first 96 hours and a summary here:
- Peak window: Jul 12 10:00–16:00 PT (expected blitz after email campaign)
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~18k (checkout flows), estimated token/sec at peak ~120k tokens/sec

We are requesting a temporary 3x rate margin for the 6-hour peak window, with automatic rollback and monitoring. Procurement copied for SLA review.

Thanks for the details — couple quick clarifying questions before I sign off on any uplift:

1) Is the 120k tokens/sec estimate accounting for streaming vs non-streaming sessions (streaming sessions hold connections longer and affect concurrency)?
2) What is the expected sequence length distribution (median / 95th) — this affects KV cache hit rate and batching efficiency.
3) Are you open to us routing non-critical validation calls to a lower-capacity model variant during the 6-hour peak? That reduces token cost and makes a smaller uplift possible.

If answers look favorable we can provision a temporary soft-limit increase on the hosted tier for RR for the stated window and implement automatic rollback + guardrails (error budgets, fallbacks). I also want to limit the uplift to the primary model family — no full model swaps without ops approval.

-David
David Kim | Product Manager, Serving Runtime
david.kim@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RapidRetail launch: traffic forecast & temporary rate uplift request

Ben / David / Lauren —

Technical proposal from Solutions:
- Warm-up: run a staged warm-up over 24 hours prior to peak. We'll pre-seed KV caches for top 500 prompt prefixes using synthetic traffic (safe tokens) — reduces cold-start token overhead by ~30–40% based on similar retail workloads.
- Batching config: enable continuous batching with 30ms collector timeout on inference nodes serving RR during peak; this should increase throughput efficiency without adding noticeable latency.
- Fallback model: route non-customer-facing health checks/validation to a 2-bit quantized variant of the same family; maintain primary model for user-facing generation.
- Monitoring & rollback: create a dashboard with token/sec, latency P95, error-rate thresholds; automatic rollback if error-rate > 2% for 5 consecutive minutes.

Numbers request for ops: if Sophie confirms 120k tokens/sec peak, we should request a temporary capacity uplift to cover 160k tokens/sec (headroom + batching variance). That aligns with a 1.3x safety margin after warm-up.

I'll put a draft runbook in the shared drive and coordinate a staging warm-up tomorrow night.

—Priyom
Priyom Das | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Approving the temporary uplift with the following conditions:
1) Uplift window: Jul 12 08:30–16:30 PT (includes 1-hour ramp up and cool down)
2) Provisioned limit: cap at 160k tokens/sec for the hosted account (as recommended by Priyom)
3) Warm-up required and validated 6 hours before peak; do not exceed synthetic warm-up token budget in runbook without product sign-off
4) Monitoring dashboard + escalation path documented and on-call engineer assigned for the window (Monica, please own)
5) Procurement: we need an SLA addendum executed before uplift — procurement@rapidretail.com pls confirm process.

Once procurement confirms and Priyom posts the runbook link I'll issue the operational uplift and schedule an ops pre-flight check at 07:30 PT on Jul 12.

-Lauren
